Bill.BriefDescription: Prohibiting local governments from limiting citizens' ability to protect their homes from fires by removing or trimming potentially dangerous trees or vegetation near their homes.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to prohibiting local governments from limitingcitizens' ability to protect their homes from fires by trimming orremoving potentially dangerous trees or vegetation near their homes;adding a new section to chapter 36.70A RCW; adding a new section tochapter 35.21 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 35.63 RCW; adding anew section to chapter 35A.63 RCW; and adding a new section to chapter36.70 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 36.70A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) No county or city may enact, enforce, or maintain an ordinance,development regulation, zoning regulation, or official control, policy,or administrative practice that prohibits the owner of a residentialdwelling with potentially flammable roofing material from trimming orremoving trees or vegetation surrounding the dwelling in all directionsin an area equal to the maximum site potential tree height for firesuppression purposes. (2) For the purposes of this section, "site potential tree height" p. 1 HB 2373means a distance equal to the height of the tallest tree that can growon that site.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) No city or town may enact, enforce, or maintain an ordinance,development regulation, zoning regulation, or official control, policy,or administrative practice that prohibits the owner of a residentialdwelling with potentially flammable roofing material from trimming orremoving trees or vegetation surrounding the dwelling in all directionsin an area equal to the maximum site potential tree height for firesuppression purposes. (2) For the purposes of this section, "site potential tree height"means a distance equal to the height of the tallest tree that can growon that site.
